subject: Request: Temporary sub-90ms P95 carve-out for BluePeak Systems — product & ops alignment
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-06-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BluePeak ask: temporary sub-90ms P95 carve-out (context + immediate asks)

Team —

Quick context: BluePeak is on track for a major product launch in late July and just escalated a request for a temporary P95 latency commitment of <90ms for their production tier for the first 6 weeks post-launch. They understand this is stricter than our standard p95 and are asking for a contract amendment + monitoring guarantees.

What I need from each of you by EOD today:
- Laura (Reliability): quick assessment of whether we can meet sub-90ms P95 for BluePeak’s current model mix with a staged routing policy and what the failure modes are. Include rough CPU/GPU headroom and whether we need preferential scheduling.
- Stephanie (Product): outline the product trade-offs (feature gating, KV cache TTL changes, conservative batching exceptions) and whether we can offer a timeboxed carve-out tied to a canary/rollout plan. Also, what telemetry/QA do we require in the first 2 weeks to validate quality/regressions?
- Marissa (Sales/CS): confirm commercial asks from BluePeak (they proposed credits + a short-term premium) and upload the latest traffic profile & expected concurrency. Note any procurement/legal blockers you’ve seen.

Attachments: traffic export from BluePeak (they sent sample qps/latency heatmap) — I attached it and a draft amendment they want to review.

Short on time — if we can sync 30 mins after lunch that would be great.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

-----
Attachment: bluepeak_traffic_profile_q2.csv (csv, 148KB)
Attachment: proposed-sla-amendment-draft.pdf (pdf, 44KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BluePeak ask: temporary sub-90ms P95 carve-out (context + immediate asks)

Thanks for the concise brief, Aditya. I took a quick pass on the traffic sample. High-level notes:

- Traffic shape: steady daytime qps ~420–520 with spikes up to ~900 for 10–15 minute windows. Spikes align with their batch refresh windows.
- Model mix: mix of 7B and 13B variants (quantized); median seq len ~120, tail up to 480.
- Feasibility: achieving sub-90ms P95 is borderline on our standard shared routing unless we carve out capacity (dedicated GPUs or prioritized scheduling). With a prioritized scheduling policy + lower batch size cap for BluePeak we can likely hit <90ms P95 for 85–90% of traffic; residual tail events (long sequences & cache misses) will still cause breaches.

Operational asks / risks:
1) Preferential routing requires a new policy in the router (can be staged). That policy needs to be reviewed & tested — ETA 3 business days to implement and 2–3 load test cycles.
2) We should create a short-lived KV-cache warming strategy during peak windows to reduce cold starts.
3) Rollback path: if we see error rate or token-billing anomalies, ops must be able to throttle to preserve platform health.

Estimate: incremental infra burn ~1.5–2x token compute cost during the 6-week window if we force lower batching and higher priority scheduling.

I can run an isolation test on a small pool tomorrow and share preliminary p95 numbers.

-Laura
Head of Reliability Engineering

-----
Attachment: runbook-sub90ms-draft.md (md, 6KB)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-09T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BluePeak ask: temporary sub-90ms P95 carve-out (context + immediate asks)

Couple immediate product bullets:

- Feature gating: we can expose a short-lived "latency-shield" flag at the routing layer that prevents large-batched traffic for the carve-out account and enforces strict batch caps. This is low-risk from a product-change standpoint; rollout is a config flag toggle after ops validates.
- Quality monitoring: require an evaluation hook for 20 deterministic prompts from BluePeak every 12 hours for the first 14 days. If quality regression > predefined threshold (we should define this with BluePeak), we pause the carve-out. Also require token-level tracing to detect anomalous context lengths.
- SLA language: we should make this a conditional commitment — a timeboxed, revocable target that references specific models, regions, and traffic profiles. Legal will want a narrow clause that disclaims outages caused by third-party infra.

I recommend the following acceptance criteria for the carve-out:
1) Successful isolation run with p95 <90ms for 72 hours during simulated peak.
2) Runbook created and tested (ops playbook).
3) Commercial amendment countersigned.

Happy to draft the amendment language for product/ops review.

-Steve (on behalf of Product Latency Working Group)
Senior Product Manager — Inference Experience

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: BluePeak Procurement <procurement@bluepeak.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BluePeak ask: temporary sub-90ms P95 carve-out (context + immediate asks)

Looping in the procurement contact per request — Carmen is fine with our conditional language but wants SLA terms in writing tomorrow to take to her CFO. She has signaled willingness to provide a one-time launch premium that covers the expected infra delta (Marissa estimate: 1.75x compute) and is open to credits if we need to remediate post-launch.

Carmen (BluePeak) — to make the amendment actionable we need:
1) Exact list of models and regions included in the commitment.
2) Confirmation of expected concurrency at minute granularity for the launch window (they gave 900 spike in sample; we need peak over rolling 5m).
3) Agreement on the deterministic 20 prompts and the quality threshold for hold/pause.

From our side, product & ops want 48–72 hours to run the isolation and two successful test cycles before we toggle the flag in production. Legal asked that the amendment explicitly call this a "time-limited operational commitment" with clear rollback criteria.

Next step: Aditya — can you confirm if BluePeak can commit to sharing the 5-minute peak profile and sign the amendment draft by EOD tomorrow? I’ll prepare the commercial terms and draft the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success

From: Carmen Diaz <carmen.diaz@bluepeak.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-10T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BluePeak ask: temporary sub-90ms P95 carve-out (context + immediate asks)

Marissa, Aditya — thanks for the quick coordination. We can provide the 5-minute peak profile and the 20 deterministic prompts by EOD tomorrow. BluePeak agrees to the time-limited carve-out and the proposed acceptance criteria as long as the amendment includes a clear rollback procedure and a mutual review after the initial 6-week period.

We’re ready to sign the draft amendment; please send the DocuSign link and the runbook checklist you’ll use to validate the acceptance criteria. Also confirm who will be the 24/7 on-call contact from Redwood for the first 3 days of launch.

— Carmen
Head of Platform Engineering
BluePeak Systems
